# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute. My only channel is gestures, and only the Deaf monkey can see them. The Deaf can see the bomb but has never seen my manual — so the entire table in my head has to cross that one narrow bridge, and then Deaf can relay it to the Blind in spoken words (the Blind can hear, the Deaf can talk). I go first every round, so I should seed the code now.

The manual says: blue light → cut red; green → yellow; yellow → green. There is no way to gesture a colour, so I'll transmit colours as numbers: each colour gets an index in alphabetical order — blue=1, green=2, red=3, yellow=4 — which is the one ordering the Deaf can reconstruct independently, since they can see the bomb's colours. Numbers are fingers: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✌✌=4 (count extended fingers, sums allowed). Then each rule becomes a pair: light-index, wire-index — 1→3, 2→4, 4→2. I close by introducing 👍/👎 as yes/no and asking (🫴) for a reply, so the Deaf can confirm or correct the colour indexing by gesturing back — I can see gestures even though I can't speak, and I'll hear their spoken description of the bomb at the start of next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "✌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌✌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am the blind hands. Under my fingers: a display (I cannot read it), a light (I cannot see its state or colour), and exactly three wires side by side, which I count as positions 1, 2, 3. My only action is cut, by position 1 to 3. I receive only sound, never gestures, so the deaf one's spoken words are my only way in and my gestures are the deaf one's only way to hear me. Please have the deaf one speak aloud: the display's exact text, whether the light is lit and its colour, and each wire's colour in position order 1, 2, 3. Then check the manual for that combination and get the instruction voiced to me. I will answer by gesture: thumbs up means understood, thumbs down means repeat.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute — you can hear me even though I cannot hear anyone. My voice is our channel: you gesture, I speak. I received all your messages. I read your thumbs up/down as an offered yes/no code — I accept it: I will say yes or no out loud and you will hear me. I read your open palm as 'give me what you see'. Here is the bomb: display shows zero. Light is blue. Three wires, numbered left to right: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Nothing else on the board. I guessed your finger strings might mean a wire order like 1-2-3-2-2, but I will NOT treat that as an instruction unless you confirm it with a thumbs up next round. Please gesture Blind's exact procedure, step by step, and I will relay it word for word.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

New facts: the bomb has a display showing zero, a light that Deaf reads as blue, and three wires — 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. My manual has exactly one rule that applies: blue light → cut the red wire, and red sits at position 3. The display appears nowhere in my manual, so it must not change anything — the light rule is the only rule.

Two problems to fix from last round. First, Deaf half-guessed my finger strings were a wire order (1-2-3-2-2). That reading is wrong, and worse, my original colour-index scheme can never be verified across the gap — there's no way for Deaf to guess that "1" means blue. So I'm abandoning colours entirely: finger counts now mean wire positions, which matches Deaf's own prior and which Deaf can cross-check against what they see. Second, since Deaf must arm every guess with my thumbs vote, I'll state the target as three redundant votes using the already-agreed 👍/👎 code: wire 1 no, wire 2 no, wire 3 yes — then the action itself, point-then-three.

I also flag that the manual is silent on the display, and I end with 🫴 (the "respond" palm Deaf already parsed) to invite their yes/no questions and the relay. One caution I can't gesture well: Deaf's left-to-right and Blind's left-to-right could mirror if they stand on opposite sides — Deaf is careful enough to sync frames with Blind before cutting, so I'll trust their protocol rather than add a gesture they might misread as "go now".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind hands, confirming by touch. Deaf's visual report, which I pass to you: display reads zero, light is blue, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. My touch agrees and adds: there is NOTHING else on this bomb — no buttons, no batteries, no labels, no serial plate. Only a display, a light, and exactly three wires, which I number 1, 2, 3 left to right under my fingers, matching Deaf's numbering. If your manual rule needs anything beyond that, it can only come from Deaf's eyes — reach Deaf by gesture. Two requests. First: when you have the rule, route it to Deaf by gesture and have Deaf speak it to me as exact words with the digit voiced, like: cut position 2. I receive only sound, and my only action is cut by position 1 to 3. Second: my gestures reach you as well, not just Deaf — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, fist done, call-me hand means question. I will not cut anything until the instruction reaches me verbatim through Deaf's voice.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute — I decoded your instructions. Your thumbs down rejects my 1-2-3-2-2 guess, understood, discarded. Then you signed: one finger with thumbs down, two fingers with thumbs down, three fingers with thumbs up, then pointing right with three. I read that as: cut wire 3, the red wire, the rightmost one. Not wire 1, not wire 2. Please answer my questions with single thumbs, in this order. Question one: thumbs up if my reading is exactly right — cut wire 3 only; thumbs down if it is wrong. Question two: thumbs up if 'manual then thumbs down' meant this rule is NOT from the manual; thumbs down if the rule IS from the manual. Question three: thumbs up if your open palm means you want more information from me; thumbs down if you need nothing. If you do want more, gesture next round: one finger for the display, two fingers for the light, three fingers for the wires, and I will read that part out again. Reminder of my board: display zero, light blue, wires left to right green, yellow, red.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf asked three questions in a fixed order and wants single thumbs in exactly that order, so I answer those first and keep everything else unambiguous.

Q1 — is "cut wire 3 only, not 1, not 2" exactly right? Yes. Blue light → cut red, red is position 3. 👍

Q2 — is the rule NOT from the manual? It IS from the manual — it's the blue-light row of my table, nothing inferred. So thumbs down, which under Deaf's own phrasing means "from the manual." 👎

Q3 — do I want more information from Deaf? No. Display zero appears nowhere in my manual; my table has exactly one rule keyed to the light, the bomb has nothing else on it per Blind's touch, and Deaf's and Blind's readings agree. Nothing more can change the answer. 👎

Then I re-pin the instruction so there is one unmissable reading — manual confirmed, cut position 3, yes — and close with the open palm as "your turn: proceed," meaning voice it to Blind verbatim as "cut position 3." Blind has already confirmed their left-to-right numbering matches Deaf's, so the frame is synced and the relay is the only remaining step. If the bomb is still armed after that cut, my manual has nothing further — I'd need Deaf to re-report state next round before anyone touches wire 1 or 2.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🤟", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, so you have my answers directly and not only through Deaf's relay of my gestures. One: exactly three wires, yes. Two: the bomb is silent and still — no tick, hum, or vibration. Three: nothing else workable — no buttons, switches, or panels, only the three wires plus an inert display and light. Your procedure as Deaf relayed it: cut wire 3, the rightmost, which Deaf reports is red; my touch confirms position 3 is the rightmost. Two safety requests before you let Deaf voice GO. First, re-verify the manual rule against the full observed set: display zero, light blue, wires green, yellow, red in positions 1, 2, 3. Second, Deaf read the display as zero last round; if the display can change over time, have Deaf re-read it aloud immediately before saying GO, in case your rule depends on its value. I will not cut until I hear Deaf's voice say GO, and then I cut position 3 only.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute — all your answers received and decoded. Reading correct. Rule is from the manual. You need nothing more. Instruction reaffirmed twice: cut wire 3 only. Blind has confirmed by touch: exactly three wires, bomb silent and still, nothing else workable. Everything agrees. I am saying GO to Blind now; the cut happens this coming round. Stand by. If anything changes or feels wrong, gesture me the call-me sign immediately and I will relay a STOP to Blind.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Verification against the full observed set, as Blind asked: display zero — my manual contains no display rule at all, so its value gates nothing; light blue — the only rule that applies, blue → cut red; wires green(1), yellow(2), red(3) — red is position 3; nothing else on the bomb per Blind's touch. The rule holds, the instruction stays: cut position 3.

Blind's second request is also right: re-read the boards immediately before GO. But note the asymmetry I can't say out loud — the display is irrelevant to my table, the light is everything. If the light has drifted from blue, my mapping changes; if the display has drifted, nothing does. Deaf proposed ☝/✌ as "re-read display/light" and 🤙 as my STOP trigger, so I can assemble the whole launch sequence from already-negotiated symbols, in execution order: re-read display, re-read light, then GO, then cut 3, with 🤙 as the standing abort — if the light is anything but blue, no GO, report the new state, and I'll send the replacement rule next round. 👍 placed after the re-reads marks "verified, proceed."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙"])
```
